interpretation_notes: Each boundary marker separates two proposed word-like or meaningful units.
Read a marked string such as Donne¦-¦le¦-¦moi as the proposed units Donne, -, le, -, moi.
Spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, and punctuation can be separate units; do not reject an example merely because these separators have been split out.
Deterministic validation has already checked that removing the boundary markers recreates the input exactly.

candidate.rationale: Focuses on imperative with clitic pronouns and their ordering.

review.explanation: The segmentation highlights an affirmative imperative with postverbal clitics: va + - + t' (te) + en, correctly showing the special t' before en and using the hyphen as its own separator. Splitting t' and en is pedagogically useful to show clitic ordering in va-t'en. Punctuation and spacing are handled acceptably.
notes: t' is the elided te before en in affirmative imperatives (me/te -> m'/t' before en/y).
Hyphen as a separate unit is fine; apostrophe remains with t', which is acceptable per guidance.
